title: CE333 : UTILITIES 1
description: LECTURE 1 reviewer on basic electrical terms, Ohm's Law, energy calculation, and cost of operation.

reviewer.title: 1. Electric Charge, Free Electrons, and Coulomb

content.text: Electric charge is carried by the electrons and proton within an atom. Electrons carry negative charge, while protons carry positive charge. Free electrons are electrons which are not attached to a specific atom and are free to move; they are sometimes called conduction electrons.

items: The SI unit of electric charge is the Coulomb (C).
One electron or proton has a charge of 1.6 x 10-19 C.
Copper is used as a universal reference conductor.
1 cubic meter of copper has 8.5 x 1028 free electrons.

content.title: Number of free electrons
content.expression: N = volume x 8.5 x 10^28;   volume = pi(d/2)^2L
content.example: For copper with d = 0.0016 m and L = 10 m, N = 1.71 x 10^24 electrons.
content.practice: A copper bus bar contains 4.18 x 10^24 electrons and has a cross section of 0.5 inch by 0.6 inch. Find its length.

content.text: Electric current is the rate of electron movement or electron flow in a given material. The SI unit of current is Coulomb per second, commonly called Ampere (A).

content.title: Electric current
content.expression: I = Q/t;   Q = It;   t = Q/I
content.example: If I = 2 A for t = 30 s, Q = It = (2)(30) = 60 C.
content.practice: A current of 4 A flows in a wire. Determine the electron flow per second.

Electromotive force (emf or voltage) is the energy provided by a cell, battery, or generator per coulomb of charge passing through it. Its SI unit is Joule per Coulomb, commonly called Volt (V).

content.title: Voltage
content.expression: V = W/Q;   W = VQ;   Q = W/V
content.example: A 100 V battery does 500 J of work. Q = W/V = 500/100 = 5 C.
content.practice: Moving 8.5 x 10^18 electrons uses 136 J. Determine the voltage.

Electric resistance is the property of a material to oppose or resist electron flow. The SI unit is the ohm (Ω). Resistance varies directly as length and inversely as cross-sectional area.

content.title: Resistance and resistivity
content.purpose: relating resistance to a conductor's material and dimensions.
content.example: For a 0.315 mm diameter wire with R = 10 Ω and ρ = 4.9 x 10^-7 Ω-m, L = RA/ρ = 1.59 m.

Electric power efficiency is the ratio of output power divided by input power.

content.title: Power efficiency
where: Pout = useful power output in watts (W)
content.example: A buzzer receives 5 J and transfers 2 J into sound. Efficiency = (2/5) x 100 = 40%.
content.practice: A toaster receives 120 J and transfers 50 J into heat. Determine its efficiency.

content.text: An electric circuit is a continuous and closed path of electric current. It consists of electric devices, a source of electricity, wires, and a switch connected together.

<svg class="ce333-diagram" viewBox="0 0 640 180" role="img" aria-label="Original closed electric circuit diagram"><rect x="70" y="48" width="90" height="55" rx="8" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/><text x="91" y="81" fill="currentColor" font-size="16">source</text><line x1="160" y1="75" x2="260" y2="75" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="3"/><circle cx="292" cy="75" r="31" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/><text x="280" y="82" fill="var(--accent)" font-size="20">L</text><line x1="323" y1="75" x2="515" y2="75" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="3"/><path d="M515 75v55H70V103" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="3"/><path d="M205 75l18 -12M205 75l18 12" stroke="var(--accent)" stroke-width="3"/><text x="252" y="160" fill="currentColor" font-size="16">closed path with switch, source, wires, and device</text></svg>

items: Direct current (DC): one-directional flow of electric charge, commonly from electrochemical cells or batteries.
Alternating current (AC): electron flow that periodically reverses; it can be produced by alternators.

content.text: Ohm's Law states that the current drawn by an electric load is directly proportional to the voltage across the load and inversely proportional to the electrical resistance.

content.title: Ohm's Law
content.expression: I = V/R;   V = IR;   R = V/I
content.example: An electric iron draws 2.5 A at 230 V. R = V/I = 230/2.5 = 92 Ω.
content.practice: A nichrome heating coil takes 30 A at 120 V. Determine its resistance.

Electric energy is a form of energy used to run or operate electrical devices. Its standard unit is the Joule (J) or kiloJoule (kJ); common units also include kiloWatt-hour (kWh) and MegaWatt-hour (MWh). Electric power is the rate of consuming electric energy. Its standard unit is the Watt (W); bigger units are kiloWatt (kW) and MegaWatt (MW).

content.title: Electric energy and power
content.example: A radio draws 0.9 A at 110 V for 30 h. Energy = 99 W x 30 h = 2.97 kWh.
content.practice: Calculate energy consumption when the power and operating time of an electrical device are given.

reviewer.title: 9. Cost of Operation of Electrical Equipment / Devices

content.title: Operating cost
where: Energy consumed = electrical energy used in kWh
content.example: A radio consumes 2.97 kWh at Php 9.72 per kWh. Cost = 2.97 x 9.72 = Php 28.87.
content.practice: Calculate the daily operating cost for the listed heater, refrigerator, microwave, and air-conditioning loads using the stated VECO rate.
